routing.reason: A small, fully specified feature (one column, two endpoints, one form field) with testable criteria and no security stake.
rulings: Ruling: workflow `direct` — criteria are already testable and one developer can do the API, the migration and the small page change in one go — cost if wrong: a missed edge case is caught by the single review, and the run can be re-routed to `default`.

Ruling: no PO, UX, architect or security step — the acceptance criteria are complete, the form field is one input in the existing page, and the date is validated input with no auth, payment or personal-data stake — cost if wrong: a validation gap would reach the review unflagged by a security pass.

Ruling: one task for `back` that covers the whole ticket — the front change is about 10 lines in public/app.js and public/index.html, and splitting it would cost more than it saves — cost if wrong: the front part gets less specialised attention.
Ruling: budget $0.80 — one developer task, the checks, the migration review and one short review round — cost if wrong: the run stops before the review and the user must raise it.

task.goal: Add an optional `due_date` to tasks. (1) src/db.ts: append a NEW migration to the `migrations` array (never edit the existing one): `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT` (nullable, no default), so existing rows get NULL. (2) src/tasks.ts: add `due_date: string | null` to `Task` and `Row`; `createTask` takes an optional due_date; `updateTask` must tell an absent `due_date` (leave unchanged) apart from an explicit `null` (clear), so do not use `??` for it; use `'due_date' in changes` or `!== undefined`. (3) src/app.ts: POST /api/tasks and PATCH /api/tasks/:id accept `due_date`; validate it as a string matching `YYYY-MM-DD` that is a real calendar date (reject `2026-1-5`, `tomorrow`, `2026-02-30`, non-strings such as numbers; round-trip the parsed UTC date to catch impossible days); on failure answer 400 `{"error": "due_date must be a date in YYYY-MM-DD format"}` and save nothing (validate before any write, in PATCH too, so a bad due_date does not apply a title or done change). `null` is valid on PATCH, and on POST it means no date. (4) public/index.html and public/app.js: add an optional `<input type="date">` with an accessible label to the add form and send it as `due_date` only when filled; show the due date next to the title when it is not null (build it with textContent, like the existing code, no innerHTML with data). (5) test/tasks.test.ts: cover the default null, create with a date, PATCH set, PATCH clear with null, PATCH without due_date leaves it, each invalid format and 2026-02-30 answering 400 with that exact body and nothing saved, and a database at the first migration upgrading with due_date null (use migrate() on a db at user_version 1 with a pre-existing row). (6) README.md: document the field, the validation and the 400 error. Run the project's checks (typecheck and tests from package.json) before finishing.

criteria.why: Migration adds nullable due_date column, Task interface and rows include it, defaulting to null.
POST passes due_date ?? null; PATCH keeps existing when undefined, sets null to clear.
validDueDate checks regex plus round-trip through Date, returns 400 with exact message before any write; tests cover bad formats, 2026-02-30, non-strings.
New ALTER TABLE migration appended; test upgrades a v1 DB and old row gets null.
Page renders 'Due <date>' span when present and the form has an optional date input sent only when set.
Tests cover default, create, patch set/keep/clear, invalid values, migration; README updated.

findings.what: Submit handler now wraps POST in try/catch and shows errors; a reasonable need for the 400 but is a small behaviour change beyond the ticket.
validDueDate accepts years like 0000 (Date parses it); unlikely to matter. Also a non-object JSON body (e.g. null) would throw on body.due_date, but that is pre-existing handling.
Inline style (due.style.flex) in JS instead of CSS.
No test for the UI changes; the loop of bad values makes many tests that each do multiple requests, a bit heavy but fine.

judge.summary: The diff meets all six criteria with a clean validation helper, a proper migration, and thorough tests including an upgrade test and no-write checks on rejected input. Only minor nits remain: the unrelated-but-sensible error handling in the form submit, inline styling, and no UI tests.
